Subject: SOC2 scope update + retention tiers for renewal

Hi Aisha / Lauren,

We're starting prep for our November renewal and the security/compliance team asked for a refreshed attestation package. Two quick asks to unblock legal and procurement: 

1) A gap list from Redwood that shows what changed in scope since our last SOC2 (particularly around log retention and cross-region replication).
2) Confirmation of the log retention tiers available (365/730/1095 days) and pricing delta for each — we expect to decide on a tier by the end of the week.

Separately, our platform growth means we may need a short-term capacity uplift (burst seats) during the audit window. Can you include recommended burst sizes and pricing?

I've attached the current scope doc we have on file and a 10k line sample from our audit team for verification.

Thanks,
Samantha

Samantha.Lee@acmetech.com

Looping in Ben and Karthik to confirm pricing and evidence details.

Hi Samantha — Ben here. Brief on pricing and capacity uplift options: 

Pricing model (summary):
- Retention tiers: +10% per additional 365 days (hot), +6% per 365 days (cold archival, 30-day recall SLA).
- Burst seats: flat daily rate scaled by GPU class. Example: +$1,200/day for 8xA10s equivalent pool (up to 20% throughput uplift).

Suggested combos:
- Conservative: Keep hot retention at 365 (no uplift) — minimal pricing delta.
- Audit-focused: Hot retention at 730 days + 14-day burst at 8xA10s — typically sufficient for bulk evidence replay and sampling; we can cap egress and indexing bandwidth.
- Full-scope: Hot 1095 + 30-day burst at 12xA10s; recommended if you expect continuous, large-volume sampling across multiple regions.

I'll prepare a short quote for the three scenarios and attach the retention cost spreadsheet. Aisha — can you confirm whether Acme prefers hot vs cold to finalize numbers?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha,

Thanks for sending the sample logs. I've reviewed and here are the items we'll include in the attestation bundle plus a short gaplist where applicable: 

Evidence bundle (what Redwood will provide):
- Control mapping doc (updated to reflect replication controls) — PDF (will attach).
- Audit-log export samples: syslog, api-auth, admin-console events (we'll provide hashed PII samples).
- Retention config export (snapshot of S3 lifecycle rules / cold archive mapping).
- Access control change history (last 12 months) and MFA enforcement report.
- Encryption-at-rest cert and KMS key rotation ledger.

Noted gaps and mitigations:
- Gap: cross-region DR test schedule not documented for the exact 30-day window requested by your auditors. Mitigation: we can provide DR runbook and last DR test summary, and schedule a focused DR test in December if you need a signed test report.
- Gap: we currently store ephemeral debug traces for 14 days by default; auditors asked for an explicit policy for retention of those traces — we'll add a policy addendum to the attestation bundle.

Required actions for Acme to expedite:
- Confirm hashed vs raw PII handling for the audit team (default: hashed).
- Confirm which retention tier you select (365/730/1095) and whether cold/hot.
- Provide a single procurement contact for the DocuSign amendment.

Attachments: redwood-retention-options-v3.xlsx (pricing & tier definitions), control-mapping-2026-11.pdf (will deliver shortly).

If you're comfortable, we can include the DR runbook and run a targeted DR test next week (we'll draft a short statement that your auditors can accept as interim evidence).

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
